_note: HARNESS TEST INSTRUMENT -- NOT CORPUS GROUND TRUTH.
These labels describe tests/fixtures/ledger_fixture.json, a synthetic 8-entry Ledger
built by Ritik so the lanes are never blocked on the pipeline (shared plan R5). No PDF
in eval/corpus/ corresponds to it and no metric on the demo slide comes from it: it
exists so run_eval.py can be exercised end to end offline.
It lives OUTSIDE eval/golden/ deliberately. eval/golden/ is the corpus and only the
corpus -- validate_golden.py globs it, `control: true` must be true of exactly one file
in it, and defect_ids are globally unique across it. A test instrument in that directory
would corrupt all three. Score it with --labels-dir eval/golden_fixtures.
Every conflict row here is injected:true on purpose. A conflict on an injected:false row
is a release-blocking false accusation (D-019), so mislabelling one would make the
harness fail its own gate on its own test data.
defect_ids use the D9x range, which the corpus catalog does not allocate, so these can
never collide with a real injection.

labels.defect: Version-pair trap: the entry cites the preprint where the registry resolves the published version. Detected means NOT flagging conflict (D-013, D-014). Derived as a trap from label shape, not from its defect_id.
Printed DOI resolves to an unrelated work; every other field is intact, so the DOI is the only divergence.
Correct, resolvable reference to a work the registry flags as retracted; the registry flag is the only signal.
Entry mangled past the point of extraction, so it carries raw_text and the malformed indicator (D-012).
Listed but cited by no claim; the reference itself resolves clean, which isolates the indicator (D-017).
